title: SRS as interchange format: a database on an SRS schema (2026-11-08)

sections.name: vignette
sections.label: Owner's words (2026-11-08, verbatim)
sections.content:
Here's an experiment.

SRS is a standalone format.
But it is also an interchange format. We don't have to build with srs directly.

Can we build a database on an srs schema?
If I built my governance engine, could I generate a database design off a set of packages? Or could I create a set of packages off my data se design?(muDemocracy-decisions was a pre srs experiment that stopped because I couldn't export)

What kinds of structures can SRS not represent?
This is the path to building the mukti-user experience... But still maintain sovereignty.

We can experiment autonomously in the lab

sections.name: context
sections.label: Context
sections.content: Said unprompted at the start of a session in the semanticops workspace. Frames SRS as an interchange format rather than only a storage format: packages as the schema source for a generated database, and the reverse, packages generated from a database design. muDemocracy-decisions (the decision-logger repo) is named as the pre-SRS experiment that stopped for lack of export. Names the limits question (what SRS cannot represent) and ties it to the multi-user experience with sovereignty kept. Authorises autonomous lab experimentation.
